source: Dehaene, Kerszberg, Changeux (1998) A neuronal model of a global workspace in effortful cognitive tasks
finding: Founding neural model. Two spaces: many specialized processors (perceptual, motor, long-term memory, evaluation, attention) and one global workspace of long-range neurons. Only one workspace representation is active at a time. The workspace is used when the specialists cannot do the task alone.
numbers: Simulated Stroop task, 200 trials, new task introduced after trial 20. Search phase about 30 trials; a stable pattern was found after about 5 to 50 trials across runs. Vigilance rule: after a correct answer V drops by 0.1 V; after an error V rises by 0.5(1-V). Weights bounded 0 to 7.
quote: only one such “workspace representation” can be active at any given time.
limits: Toy network on one task. Authors call it partial and incomplete. No fit to human data in the paper; predictions only.
agent_relevance: Template for a code-run workspace: one item active, chosen by competition, with a vigilance counter that opens the workspace after errors (matches G1: doubt on a signal).

source: Dehaene, Kerszberg, Changeux (1998) Stroop simulation: routine versus effortful phases
finding: Workspace activity is absent for routine tasks, appears when a new task is introduced, varies randomly while a rule is searched, is high during effortful execution, fades as the task routinizes, and returns sharply after an error. The workspace works by amplifying the relevant processor (color) and suppressing the irrelevant one (word) through descending links.
numbers: Eight listed properties (i to viii). Color naming and word naming (routine) needed no workspace. Color naming with word interference (effortful) needed it. An error trial leads to intense reactivation. Delayed-response versions need the workspace even for the routine task.
limits: Dlpfc and anterior cingulate were named as workspace sites by prediction, not tested in this paper.
agent_relevance: Maps to S0 routing: easy items go the fast path; the slow, serial, code-controlled path opens on a new task, a failed check, or an error.

source: Dehaene, Kerszberg, Changeux (1998) Selection by gating and the five processor types
finding: Inputs reach the workspace only through gating: workspace neurons send descending signals that amplify some processor inputs and extinguish others. Workspace content can then be evaluated, stored, used to guide action and reported. Random replacement of a negatively evaluated item acts as a generator of diversity that tests hypotheses.
numbers: Five processor classes: perceptual, motor, long-term memory, evaluation, attention. Global modulation by vigilance signals (awake: workspace on; slow-wave sleep: off).
limits: Descriptive architecture. No quantitative fit to human data in this paper.
agent_relevance: Selection is separate from broadcast. In our agent code does the gating and the restart on a negative evaluation; the model only fills a slot.

source: Dehaene, Kerszberg, Changeux (1998) Brain-imaging predictions made by the model
finding: The model predicts activation in areas with dense long-range connections; dlPFC and anterior cingulate fit: active in effortful tasks with graded activation by difficulty, decreasing with automatization, returning with novelty, tight to errors, and persisting during delays.
numbers: Cites imaging studies (Stroop, Wisconsin card sorting) but gives no new data or effect sizes.
limits: Anatomical claims were later contested: the Cogitate preprint found prefrontal category information but little orientation information.
agent_relevance: Ties workspace load to novelty and errors. A cheap signal for S0: use the slow path more after a failed check, less after a run of passes.

source: Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux, Dehaene (2020) Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis
finding: Twenty-year summary of the global neuronal workspace (GNW). Defines ignition: a sudden, all-or-none, self-sustained activation of a subset of workspace neurons that makes content globally available. Separates access consciousness from phenomenal consciousness and says GNW addresses access.
numbers: Divergence between seen and unseen trials at about 200 to 300 ms after stimulus onset. The first 200 ms of processing can be fully preserved on unseen trials.
quote: Ignition is characterized by the sudden, coherent, and exclusive activation of a subset of workspace neurons coding for the current conscious content
limits: Authors are the theory's proponents. The review admits rival readings of the early negativity (VAN at about 260 ms) and of the P300.
agent_relevance: Gives the working definition of the mechanism we copy: competition, sudden commitment, sustained broadcast, and a lag between local processing and global access.

source: Noel et al. (2018) and Sanchez et al. (2019) cross-modal EEG ignition, as reported in Mashour et al. (2020)
finding: Late sudden ignition after 200 ms was the only signature shared across auditory, visual and audiovisual trials (Noel 2018). A decoder trained to separate perceived from unperceived stimuli generalized across vision, hearing and touch (Sanchez 2019), including late activity in other sensory areas, read as top-down broadcast.
numbers: Trial counts and accuracies are not in the review text I read; only the qualitative result.
limits: Secondary report. The original papers were not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Supports one shared format across modules; our single typed state record is the analogue.

source: van Vugt et al. (2018) monkey V1, V4 and prefrontal recordings, as reported in Mashour et al. (2020)
finding: Perceived and missed weak stimuli both drove V1 and V4, but only perceived stimuli (hits and false alarms) gave sudden, strong, sustained prefrontal activity. Missed stimuli gave a transient decaying response. Very weak stimuli were lost between V1 and V4; stronger ones reached V4 but not frontal cortex. The signal-detection threshold matched the prefrontal ignition threshold.
numbers: Four trial types: hits, misses, correct rejections, false alarms. Spontaneous prefrontal ignitions occurred on false-alarm trials. Pre-stimulus firing and EEG state predicted false alarms.
limits: Reported via the review (original not opened). Monkeys; report was a saccade, so report and perception stay entangled.
agent_relevance: A false alarm is an ignition without a real input. A committed workspace item is not evidence that it is true (G3, G4).

source: Mashour et al. (2020) Anesthesia, disorders of consciousness and sleep as tests of the GNW
finding: Anesthetics of different classes converge on disrupting prefrontal-posterior long-range connectivity and late activity. In sleep, the first about 200 ms of sensory processing is kept but the late P3 wave to a rare sound is lost. In unresponsive patients, long-range connectivity is reduced.
numbers: Qualitative in the review text; no pooled effect size.
limits: No drug-invariant signature is proven. Focal lesions rarely abolish consciousness, which the authors explain by distributed workspace neurons; this makes the claim hard to falsify.
agent_relevance: Local processors continue without the workspace. Sub-steps can run fine while global integration (the final answer step) fails; test integration separately from steps.

source: Mashour et al. (2020) GNW compared with IIT, recurrent processing and higher-order theories
finding: GNW is a representational, architecture-based theory with specified neurons; IIT is a mathematical theory about phi. Early recurrent loops in visual areas (RPT) may match the early awareness negativity; global recurrent processing matches the late positivity.
numbers: Table 1 of the review gives qualitative contrasts. Late (about 300 ms) global ignition is the GNW marker; perturbational complexity is an IIT-linked marker.
limits: Written by GNW proponents, so the framing of rivals is theirs.
agent_relevance: Rivals do not give a build recipe; GNW does. This is a reason to use GNW as an architecture analogue only.

source: Mashour et al. (2020) Working memory as the attended item in the workspace
finding: Proposal: the attended working-memory item is conscious and uses the workspace; other items are held by weaker local persistent firing or activity-silent synaptic traces and become conscious only when reinstated as global sustained firing. Links GNW to Cowan and Oberauer focus-of-attention models.
numbers: Focus capacity is one item; a few more sit outside the focus (no number given in this review).
limits: Contested by activity-silent evidence (see Trubutschek 2017 line). Capacity numbers come from other theories.
agent_relevance: Keep exactly one active item in the broadcast slot and park others in memory; reinstate by an explicit retrieval step. Link to the Working memory subfield.

source: Mashour et al. (2020) Conscious access versus attention, and the limits of the account
finding: The review separates attention (selection that amplifies features across areas) from conscious access (global availability). It names open issues: report confounds, VAN versus P300, and phenomenal consciousness. Subliminal stimuli can evoke activity lasting over one second, but as a slowly decaying wave rather than ignition.
numbers: Qualitative; no pooled numbers.
limits: The phenomenal versus access debate is not settled by this evidence; IIT proponents reject the access view.
agent_relevance: For an agent only access matters: whether content can be used by many parts. No stance on experience is needed.

source: Baars (1988) A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness
finding: Original theory: unconscious specialist processors run in parallel; they compete for a limited-capacity global workspace (blackboard or theatre); the winning content is broadcast to all processors. Consciousness is the broadcast. The workspace is needed for novel tasks and for coordination of specialists.
numbers: Not read this session; no numbers recorded. Described as reported in Mashour et al. (2020) and Butlin et al. (2023).
limits: Psychological theory. Claims (broadcast, limited capacity) were made precise later by Dehaene and by AI authors.
agent_relevance: Source of the architecture analogue: parallel specialists, competition, one broadcast item.

source: Del Cul, Baillet, Dehaene (2007) Brain dynamics underlying the nonlinear threshold for access to consciousness
finding: Backward masking of a 16 ms digit. Subjective visibility and objective performance both followed one sigmoid in target-mask delay (SOA). Early ERP components (P1, N1) were unchanged by SOA. A late component starting about 270 to 300 ms after the target rose sigmoidally with visibility and spread over a broad fronto-parieto-temporal network.
numbers: N = 12 (from the F tests). SOAs 16, 33, 50, 66, 83, 100 ms. Seen rate rises with SOA, F(5,55) = 154.17, p < 0.001. Objective task F(5,50) = 82.02, p < 0.001; chance only at 16 ms. Objective threshold mean 40.8 ms (SD 12.4). Subjective versus objective thresholds r squared = 0.747, slope 1.03. At SOA 50 ms seen and unseen trials diverge from about 270 ms; target-present unseen ERPs still exceed mask-only ERPs.
limits: Small N. One paradigm (digit, masking). Report-based, so post-perceptual task effects are not removed (see Pitts 2014).
agent_relevance: Shows the nonlinear all-or-none threshold: the input changes smoothly, yet access flips. Analogue: a commit gate with a threshold, not a soft average.

source: Gaillard et al. (2009) Converging intracranial markers of conscious access
finding: Intracranial EEG while patients saw masked or unmasked words. Masked (unseen) words gave early brief local activity with gamma but no long-distance coherence. Seen words gave late, long-lasting, widespread activity with increased beta phase synchrony and Granger causality between distant electrodes.
numbers: N = 10 implanted patients. Masked forced-choice d' mean 0.02 (range -0.18 to 0.27). Mean effect duration 60 ms masked versus 378 ms unmasked (p < 10^-6); mean onset 366 ms versus 522 ms. Beta synchrony at 300 to 500 ms for unmasked words: t(1,282 df) = 7.12, p < 10^-10; none for masked.
limits: Epilepsy patients; uneven coverage so coherence was computed only within a patient. Authors call the oscillation analysis exploratory; the theory does not fix a frequency band.
agent_relevance: Unseen items still run a feed-forward cascade but dissipate; seen items persist and synchronize. Sub-results that never enter the shared state record have no influence on later steps.

source: Bekinschtein et al. (2009) Neural signature of the conscious processing of auditory regularities (local-global paradigm)
finding: Five-sound series. Local deviants (last sound differs) gave a mismatch negativity at about 130 ms, the same whether subjects counted, mind-wandered or did a visual task. Global deviants (violating the series rule) gave a late effect from about 260 ms that vanished when attention was drawn away. The global effect marks conscious processing.
numbers: Exp 1: 11 volunteers counting; global effect 260 to 700 ms. Exp 2: 11 mind-wandering; global effect gone beyond 400 ms. Exp 3: 10 with visual task; no measurable global effect. Noticed the rare series: 3 of 11 passive, 0 in the interference group. Local effect in 32 of 32 subjects. Patients: 3 of 4 minimally conscious showed a global effect and later became fully conscious; 0 of 4 vegetative.
limits: Patient sample of 8, so diagnostic claims are provisional. Later work reports some global effects without attention (not read here).
agent_relevance: Clean dissociation: local automatic prediction error needs no workspace; a rule spanning time does. Give multi-step rule checks to the slow path only.

source: Pitts, Lutsyshyna, Hillyard (2014) Isolating neural correlates of conscious perception from neural correlates of reporting
finding: Counter-evidence to the late-ignition marker. In inattentional blindness and masking with task-relevant versus task-irrelevant stimuli, the P3b and late positivity appeared only when stimuli were task-relevant, even when stimuli were clearly seen. The visual awareness negativity (about 200 to 240 ms) tracked awareness regardless of task. So the P3b may reflect post-perceptual processing and report.
numbers: Masking study: 26 recruited, 18 analysed (3 artifact, 5 aware of 16 ms colour stimuli). Behavioral SOAs 16.67, 33.34, 50, 66.67, 300 ms; EEG used 16.67 and 300 ms. Only CIN, SEC and VAN were present in aware and absent in unaware conditions regardless of task. A P3b appeared once in an unaware, task-relevant condition (colour).
limits: Small samples; a small P3b in aware task-irrelevant trials may sit below threshold (authors say so). Proponents reply that frontal ignition can occur without overt report; unresolved.
agent_relevance: Caution: what looks like a global commit may partly be the cost of reporting. Do not treat the answer-writing step as evidence the earlier state was sound.

source: Trubutschek et al. (2017) A theory of working memory without consciousness or sustained activity
finding: Participants located a masked square after 2.5 to 4 s. They did so above chance on trials rated unseen. Seen trials showed sustained alpha/beta desynchronization and decodable location; unseen trials did not. Information can be kept with no sustained global activity, which challenges the claim that all working memory lives in the workspace.
numbers: N = 17 (MEG). Seen trials 69.1% correct (SD 17.4), chance 5%. Seen versus unseen: F(1,16) = 198.5, p < 0.001, partial eta squared 0.925. 13 subjects showed above-chance blindsight (chance 25% with +-2 position tolerance). Detection d' 1.5 (SD 0.7). A distractor on 50% of trials had no effect.
limits: Unseen-trial performance is low. Miscategorized visibility reports cannot be fully excluded. Fits an activity-silent model rather than refuting the workspace.
agent_relevance: Supports separating the active broadcast item from silent stored items. The memory store holds lessons silently; they enter the prompt only on an explicit trigger.

source: Cogitate Consortium (2023 preprint; Nature 2025) Adversarial collaboration, GNWT versus IIT: prediction 1, content decoding
finding: Preregistered test. GNWT predicts prefrontal cortex is necessary for conscious content. Category (face versus object) was decodable in prefrontal cortex in all three modalities, supporting GNWT. Orientation was decodable in posterior cortex but not in prefrontal cortex in iEEG and fMRI, which favours IIT. Adding prefrontal data did not improve decoding.
numbers: 256 subjects (fMRI 120, MEG 102, iEEG 34). Optimization on 1/3 of MEG (N=32) and fMRI (N=35), then replication on MEG N=65 and fMRI N=73. Hit rate 96.84%, false alarms 1.45%. fMRI cross-task category decoding about 75% posterior and about 60% prefrontal. Stimuli 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 s; 4 categories; 20 identities.
limits: Numbers are from the 2023 preprint; the 2025 journal version may differ. Stimuli were suprathreshold, so this tests content and duration, not the ignition threshold.
agent_relevance: Prefrontal areas hold coarse category but not fine detail. The broadcast item should be a compact summary; keep fine detail in the specialist step and fetch on demand.

source: Cogitate Consortium (2023 preprint) Prediction 2: maintenance of content over time
finding: GNWT predicted a brief prefrontal ignition at stimulus onset and again at offset, with silent storage in between. No prefrontal electrode showed the onset-and-offset pattern. Posterior cortex showed sustained activity that tracked stimulus duration, as IIT predicted. This challenges the offset-ignition part of GNWT.
numbers: iEEG 31 patients; 657 posterior and 655 prefrontal electrodes. 194 of 657 (29.5%) posterior and 123 of 655 (18.7%) prefrontal responded. 25 posterior electrodes tracked duration (12 non-selective, 13 category-selective). Prefrontal: 114 onset-only, 1 early onset-offset, 0 in the predicted window (over 0.3 s). The test did detect the pattern in 10 striate or extrastriate electrodes.
quote: none of the 655 electrodes tested matched the temporal profile predicted by GNWT (i.e., onset and offset).
limits: Sparse clinically driven coverage. Alpha-band results inconclusive. GNW proponents' reply that the test over-specified the theory was not read here.
agent_relevance: A failed prediction about the workspace update at offset. Do not add a re-broadcast at every state exit on GWT grounds.

source: Cogitate Consortium (2023 preprint) Prediction 3: long-range prefrontal connectivity
finding: Neither theory passed on the preregistered phase-consistency analysis. Exploratory amplitude-based connectivity analyses matched GNWT timing (about 0.3 s) and gamma band for prefrontal links in iEEG and fMRI. IIT's V1/V2 connectivity was present but not sustained.
numbers: iEEG connectivity subjects: 4 for IIT regions, 21 for GNWT regions; MEG N=65. Category-selective synchrony below 25 Hz in V1/V2 and prefrontal.
limits: GNWT support came from exploratory, non-preregistered metrics, so it is weak. V1/V2 iEEG coverage was sparse.
agent_relevance: Overall verdict is mixed: GNWT is neither confirmed nor refuted. Treat it as a design analogue, not a proven account.

source: Sergent, Baillet, Dehaene (2005) Timing of the brain events underlying access to consciousness during the attentional blink
finding: Attentional blink with EEG. Early sensory components were the same for seen and missed second targets; a late component appeared only when the target was seen. Reported as all-or-none rather than graded.
numbers: Not read this session; no numbers recorded. Cited in Mashour et al. (2020), which says early activity is preserved under inattention.
limits: Report-based contrast, so open to the Pitts 2014 critique.
agent_relevance: The blink is a serial bottleneck: while one item holds the workspace a second can be missed. Argues for one item at a time in the commit slot.

source: Dehaene and Changeux (2011) Experimental and theoretical approaches to conscious processing
finding: Main GNW review before 2020. Summarizes masking, attentional blink and local-global results and the spiking-network simulations of ignition under masking and inattention (Dehaene, Sergent, Changeux 2003).
numbers: Not read this session; no numbers recorded. Described via Mashour et al. (2020).
limits: Superseded in part by the 2020 review and by the adversarial tests.
agent_relevance: Cite for the ignition simulation: graded input, sudden global state.

source: Goyal et al. (2022) Coordination among neural modules through a shared global workspace (ICLR 2022)
finding: Neural-network version of the workspace. Specialists compete for write access to a few memory slots by key-query attention; slot contents are then broadcast to all specialists. Cost grows linearly with the number of specialists instead of quadratically. Used in Transformers and recurrent independent mechanisms.
numbers: Bouncing balls, SCOFF baseline ARI 0.276; with workspace: 2 slots 0.154, 4 slots 0.487, 5 slots 0.915, 8 slots 0.891, 10 slots 0.351. Atari: median score ratio 1.13 (game A) and 1.11 (game B) over baseline. Hard competition with k = 5 writers on CATER. Slots stay under 10, like human working memory.
quote: specialists compete for write access to the shared workspace
limits: Vision and toy physics, not language reasoning. Performance is non-monotonic in slot count. Butlin et al. note the modules are tokens or patches, not truly separate specialists.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a small competitive shared bottleneck helps coordination and that its size matters: tune the broadcast width, do not assume bigger is better.

source: VanRullen and Kanai (2021) Deep learning and the Global Workspace Theory
finding: Opinion and roadmap. Proposes a global latent workspace: networks trained on different tasks or senses, joined by unsupervised translation between their latent spaces trained with cycle-consistency, so the workspace is amodal. Lists benefits: cross-modal grounding, robustness to out-of-distribution input, flexible control.
numbers: No experiments in this paper; roadmap only.
limits: Position paper under review. How to train the attention that selects what enters the workspace is left open.
agent_relevance: A way to keep specialist outputs in a common format. For us the common format is a typed record that code can compare.

source: Devillers, Maytie, VanRullen (2024) Semi-supervised multimodal representation learning through a global workspace
finding: Frozen unimodal image and text models are joined by a shared workspace trained with translation, contrastive and cycle-consistency losses. The workspace aligned and translated between modalities with far less matched data and could use unpaired data.
numbers: Abstract: 4 to 7 times less paired data than full supervision on two vision-language datasets. With 20% paired COCO data, the contrastive-only model reached 50.3% (+-0.2) against 55.7% (+-0.2) with the full loss set. Fixed N = 5,000 paired with varying unpaired M was tested.
limits: Small synthetic and COCO tasks, frozen encoders; no reasoning test. Gains come from cycle-consistency losses, which are not unique to workspace theory.
agent_relevance: Little direct use for a language scaffold. Lesson: a shared interface space cuts the need for pairwise adaptation between modules.

source: Butlin et al. (2023) Consciousness in artificial intelligence: insights from the science of consciousness (GWT indicators)
finding: Turns GWT into four indicators for AI: GWT-1 parallel specialist modules; GWT-2 limited-capacity workspace with selective attention; GWT-3 global broadcast to all modules, which needs recurrence; GWT-4 state-dependent attention that lets the workspace query modules in succession. Notes there is no all-or-none ignition in self-attention.
numbers: Qualitative indicator list. Paper concludes that current systems fail to meet all four. Perceiver and PaLM-E are judged short of the full set.
quote: there is nothing akin to the binary ignition process in global workspace theory in self-attention
limits: The checklist is the authors' reading; they flag four open questions (which modules, how close to ignition, multiple workspaces, selection versus uptake).
agent_relevance: A spec check for our scaffold: parallel attempts (GWT-1), one slot (GWT-2), same record visible to every step (GWT-3), code-driven next query (GWT-4).

source: Butlin et al. (2023) Assessment of Goyal et al. and VanRullen and Kanai as GWT implementations
finding: The translation roadmap is unbuilt and faces the question of how to train the attention that picks which modules write to the workspace. The shared-workspace Transformers use key-query attention to select writers and broadcast to all, but their modules are sequence tokens, not specialised subsystems, so GWT-1 is doubtful.
numbers: No experiment numbers; qualitative judgement. Neither work produced a system meeting all four indicators, though the authors call this a realistic objective.
limits: Judgement by a consciousness-science group, not a benchmark.
agent_relevance: Existing AI workspaces test the bottleneck idea, not the specialist idea. A scaffold with distinct operator roles is closer to GWT-1.

source: Butlin et al. (2023) GWT and System-2 thought: function of the workspace
finding: GWT advocates tie the workspace to extended controlled processing (System 2): the workspace keeps a goal and short summaries of interim conclusions and passes queries and responses between modules. Common code across modules also allows cross-modal analogy.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: The System-2 link is argued by authors (Kahneman 2011, VanRullen and Kanai 2021, Goyal and Bengio 2022), not tested here.
agent_relevance: Matches the plan for a controlled serial path: goal plus compact interim summaries, with queries sent by code. Link to the Dual-process theory subfield.
